title: A cantilever of a general beam profile: Timoshenko and Euler–Bernoulli tip deflections
source: Cantilever under end loads: S. P. Timoshenko and J. M. Gere, Mechanics of Materials, Van Nostrand 1972 (bending P L³/(3 E I), Saint-Venant twist T L/(G J)); the shear deflection P L/(G A_s) of the Timoshenko beam, S. P. Timoshenko, Phil. Mag. 41:744-746, 1921; G = E/(2(1 + ν))

quantities.quantity: Timoshenko beam: tip stretch u_x, N L/(E A)
quantities.reason: round-off only: the two-node beam's stiffness is the exact flexibility of a beam under end loads (interdependent interpolation, Friedman and Kosmatka 1993; with no shear flexibility the Hermite element)

quantities.quantity: Timoshenko beam: tip deflection u_y across the width, P_y L³/(3 E I_z) + P_y L/(G A_s,y)
quantities.reason: round-off only: the two-node beam's stiffness is the exact flexibility of a beam under end loads (interdependent interpolation, Friedman and Kosmatka 1993; with no shear flexibility the Hermite element)

quantities.quantity: Timoshenko beam: tip deflection u_z across the height, P_z L³/(3 E I_y) + P_z L/(G A_s,z)
quantities.reason: round-off only: the two-node beam's stiffness is the exact flexibility of a beam under end loads (interdependent interpolation, Friedman and Kosmatka 1993; with no shear flexibility the Hermite element)

quantities.quantity: Timoshenko beam: tip twist θ_x, T L/(G J)
quantities.reason: round-off only: the two-node beam's stiffness is the exact flexibility of a beam under end loads (interdependent interpolation, Friedman and Kosmatka 1993; with no shear flexibility the Hermite element)

quantities.quantity: Euler–Bernoulli beam: tip deflection u_y, P_y L³/(3 E I_z) (no shear term)
quantities.reason: as timoshenko_width; the shear terms (3.8 % and 9.4 % of the Timoshenko deflections) are absent

quantities.quantity: Euler–Bernoulli beam: tip deflection u_z, P_z L³/(3 E I_y)
Euler–Bernoulli beam: tip twist θ_x, T L/(G J)
